description: HAL USART2 (PA2/PA3, 115200 8N1) line echo through a CH340 USB-to-TTL adapter: banner, then 'echo N: <line>' for every line typed in the PC's COM port
expect:
72 MHz. USART2 PA2 (TX, AF push-pull) / PA3 (RX, input pull-up), 115200 8N1 (PCLK1 36 MHz: BRR 19 + 8/16 = 115384.6 baud, +0.16 %, as on real silicon). Wiring: PA2 -> CH340 RXD, PA3 <- CH340 TXD, GND, CH340 logic jumper at 3.3 V; the CH340's COM port opened at 115200 8N1. Once after reset: 'CH340 echo on USART2 (115200 8N1)
'. Then every line received on USART2 (ended by CR or LF; empty lines ignored; at most 63 characters kept) is answered right after its terminator with 'echo N: <line>
' (N counts the lines from 1). A COM port opened at another baud shows garbage, exactly like a real adapter.

circuit: CH340 module: not placed on this bench (the checks runner cannot place it; the COM-port round trip is covered by tests/devices/comm-firmware.test.ts) — the scenario types into USART2 directly
USART2: virtual terminal on PA2 (TX) / PA3 (RX)
